description.narrative: The Programme MENA Feminist Power in Action for Women’s Economic Rights (Fem PAWER) will strengthen young women who face multiple discrimination1 of economic gender-based violence (E/GBV) in the MENA specific countries (Jordan, Lebanon, Palestine and Tunisia) to be the leader for change by holding duty bearers accountable and improve conditions for young women in the informal sector. This through strengthening women economic empowerment (WEE), in this Programme reflected through leadership strengthening, challenging prevailing social norms and hence gender equality, and promoting women’s economic rights (WER).

The overall goal of the Program is: Gender-responsive accountability mechanisms for WEE (Women Economic Empowerment) at multiple levels in MENA specific countries (Jordan, Lebanon, Occupied Palestinian Territories and Tunisia) are established.A framework of four interlinked and mutually reinforcing intermediate changes have been identified and designed to enable progress for gender-responsive accountability based on the needs of young women.- Outcome 1 is to establish safe and secure space for the young women and WROs to develop mobilization and advocacy strategies to hold decisions makers accountable.- Outcome 2 is addressing innovative and inclusive learning / leadership for all level of the Consortium and Program.- Outcome 3 is addressing target-led capacities in advocacy, alliance building, social mobilization and inclusive leadership for young women and the WROs that will be the Partner Organizations of the Program.- Outcome 4 is addressing the target led mobilization and advocacy interventions at multiple levels.

Young women champions for Women Economic Rights: The Programme will directly target young women with disability, and rural / refugees (20 per country and around 80 in the region) to become ‘champions’ to organise, both, country and regional networks in tackling E/GBV and promote WER. Women Rights Organisations: Local CBOs and plural in/formal networks are the most vital actor in the Programme. Approximately 12 local WROs per country will be selected representing the diversity of the WRO landscape in each country. The aim is that they further will engage young women within their communities to become engaged in parts of the Programme through subgranting.

When we put the target, we did not desegregate between "women led" vs. "women and youth led". Upon selecting the CSOs, we identified those that are both women and youth led, and we reported on them accordingly in the "actual value".

A total of 3 women & youth led organizations (sub granted by AWO) had their capacities built in 2022 to advance women's right. First, 2 out of 3 CSOs conducted community research on EGBV. Second, a workshop on Advocacy strategizing (Strategic Effectiveness Methodology on advocacy and lobbying) was organized, where CSO used their research findings to build their advocacy campaigns.

During Y1 of the program, the consortium plans to release a call for applications for CSOs to apply and be part of the program, develop the selection criteria, and identify and select CSOs who will be part of FemPawer. FemPawer program adopts a bottom up approach, in which we mean having representatives of CSOs (referred to as women’s rights organisations) influencing the programme and technical support in the consortium. In this way they are more than consultative roles, they have actual influential power. This bottom up approach further includes evidence-based research, aims to contribute to the lacking knowledge base of gender responsive accountability mechanisms for E/GBV and WER for young women in the informal sector. By supporting target-led activities throughout, the Programme will ensure that discriminated young women will become advocates in their own rights, advocates that address relevant solutions and recommendations.In Year 1, AWO (tier 1, consortium partner), plans to identify 12 CSO (tier 2) to be part of FemPawer network in Jordan.

Following the release of a call for proposal and developing a selection criterion, AWO identified and selected 9 women lead grassroot organizations to be part of FemPawer network in Jordan.AWO ensured geographical coverage when selecting CSO (many of them are based in rural areas, with limited access to funding), as well as diversified its portfolio by selecting organizations that works with women with disabilities, rural women, working in the informal sector and refugee women.Also counting here AWO, as the strategic CSO partner of FemPawer in Jordan.
In Year 2, AWO (tier 1, consortium partner), plans to continue working with 9 women lead CSO (tier 2) who are part of FemPawer network in Jordan. (language:English)

In Y2, AWO signed sub-agreements with 9 women led CSOs. A launch workshop was organized to launch the partnership, network, and communicate to all donor reporting requirements. AWO worked closely with each CSO to build their financial and reporting capabilities. AWO organized one workshop on report writing to build the CSO capacities. Also, AWO organized a team building activity to enhance the relationships and networking among partners.Also counting here AWO, as the strategic CSO partner of FemPawer in Jordan.
In Year 3, AWO (tier 1, consortium partner), plans to continue working with the 9 women lead CSO (tier 2) who are part of FemPawer network in Jordan.

Therefore, in 2023 we are only counting new individuals reached through the program.During 2023, new individuals from partner organizations received trainings, coaching and took part in discussions to advance women's right and gender equality. Trainings included but are not limited to: mobile journalism, policy brief development, integrated security and wellbeing etc.

As per the donor guidelines, this indicator reflects unique individuals. Therefore, in 2024 we are only counting new individuals reached through the program.During 2024, we continued working with the same women activists and partner organization staff through mentoring, coaching, and strategizing together on how to advance the women’s economic rights agenda. Debriefing and wellbeing activities also continued, as they have proven to be an important and meaningful way to bring us all together. Through both documented feedback and observations, we can see that the women in the FemPawer network are now better equipped with the knowledge and skills needed for lobbying and advocacy.

As per the project proposal,the Programme will directly target young women with disability, and rural / refugees (20 per country (Lebanon, Jordan, Palestine, Tunisia)) to become ‘champions’ to organise, both, country and regional networks in tackling E/GBV and promote WER.Also, during Y2 of the program, it is planned to conduct a training of trainers on Integrated Security and Wellbeing, where 8 women from Jordan are planned to attend.

During 2022, AWO launched Darbuna Network for young women champions. The network aims at lobbying and advocacy to end the economic violence against young women in the informal sector. The network is composed of 22 young women with intersecting identities (disabled women, refugee women, women working in informal sector). One meeting was organized with the network, to set the structure of the network, define the network objectives and discuss what is economic gender-based violence and what forms it can take.Also, during Y2, 7 women from Jordan attended a regional training of trainers on Integrated Security and Wellbeing.

AWO actively engaged in the Universal Periodic Review (UPR) process, contributing an individual report and collaborating on three collective reports. These reports cast a spotlight on the status of women in Jordan, addressing critical areas such as women's economic participation, which is alarmingly low globally, challenges within the Personal Status Law, the prevalence of Gender-Based Violence, and the constriction of civic space.

title.narrative: # of laws blocked, adopted or improved to promote women’s economic rights, empowerment and entrepreneurship

comment.narrative: The number is extracted from the baseline evaluation report.

Counting of laws, policies and strategies in Jordan that will be blocked, adopted or improved to promote gender-responsive accountability mechanisms for women’s economic rights (WER) and empowerment of women and women rights organisations’ (WORs) involved in the Programme.

Achieving tangible changes in laws and policies often requires significant time and collective efforts. While we may not have directly changed laws within the reporting period, our initiatives have played a crucial role in raising awareness among rights holders and local authorities regarding women's economic rights.Our advocacy efforts have brought various discussions to the table, including topics such as women's right to inheritance, ensuring safe transportation to work, and addressing harassment in the workplace. By engaging in dialogue and advocacy, we have initiated important conversations and highlighted the importance of addressing these issues to promote gender equality and women's empowerment.
